source_contract.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg–de Vries equation
source_contract.source_statement: For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. Theorems 4.2–4.3: for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (Theorem 4.3 uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). Theorem 5.1 for s>1/2 and Theorem 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. Theorem 6.5: for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.
hypotheses: Real mean-zero source data in dot H^s, s>=0, and a finite positive time interval.
The bound for the dot H^s flow uses only an upper bound for the initial L2 and dot H^s norms.
For the last Lipschitz estimate theta is in (-1,0] and the two initial L2 norms have sum at most B.
source_contract.notation_map: Source Fourier norms agree with our homogeneous normalized norms. Source physical equation has the opposite dispersive sign; reflection with sign is proved in N001. Its twist is an isometry.

source_contract.source_statement: Let alpha_s in [0,1] and 0<=a_s<=b_s with b_s-a_s<=1. For three functions g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^alpha_s) with partial_t g_j in L^infinity([a_s,b_s];H^(-23/14)), define Csrc(g1,g2,g3)=integral_(a_s)^(b_s) exp(t partial_x^3) Pnz{Pnz[(exp(-t partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-t partial_x^3)g2)]*(exp(-t partial_x^3)Dinv g3)}dt. With source unnormalized norms and ||g||_Xsrc=||g||_(L^infinity L2src)+||g'||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14)), Proposition 3.4 gives ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C*(b_s-a_s)*product_j||g_j||_Xsrc+C*||g_i||_(L^infinity Hsrc^(-23/14))*product_(j!=i)||g_j||_(L^infinity L2src) for each i=1,2,3. If the three inputs are time-independent then ||Csrc||_(L2src)<=C_alpha_s*(b_s-a_s)^alpha_s*product_j||g_j||_(Hsrc^alpha_s). Constants are independent of interval location and Fourier support.
hypotheses: alpha_s in [0,1], 0<=a_s<=b_s and interval length at most one.
The three inputs have the specified L^infinity H^alpha_s regularity and time derivatives in L^infinity H^(-23/14); the static estimate requires time-independent inputs.

source_contract.source_statement: Let 0<sigma_s<=1, tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t in [t_j,t_j+tau_s]. For time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s define Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t exp(s partial_x^3)*partial_x[(exp(-s partial_x^3)g1)(exp(-s partial_x^3)g2)]ds. With beta0=2*sigma_s-3/2 for sigma_s<1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsilon for sigma_s=1/2 (any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0), and beta0=sigma_s-1 for sigma_s>1/2, Lemma 7.2 gives, for beta in [beta0,1+sigma_s], ||Fsrc_j(t;g1,g2)||_(Hsrc^beta)<=C*tau_s^((1+sigma_s-beta)/(1+sigma_s-beta0))*||g1||_(Hsrc^sigma_s)*||g2||_(Hsrc^sigma_s), with C depending only on exponents (and epsilon) and uniform in j,tau_s,t and support. Its formula (7.3) is (1/6)[S_(-s) Pnz((S_s Dinv g1)(S_s Dinv g2))]_(s=t_j)^(s=t).
hypotheses: 0<sigma_s<=1 and time-independent mean-zero g1,g2 in Hsrc^sigma_s.
tau_s>0, t_j=j*tau_s>=0 and t lies in the step.
beta0 and beta are chosen in the displayed cases and interval; epsilon is fixed positive and small in the middle case.
